name: @amparo/contracts
description: Amparo - Compact circuits for a private whistleblowing channel (Midnight Hackathon BA).
comment:dependencies: compact-runtime is pinned exactly to the runtime-version reported by
src/managed/case_admission/compiler/contract-info.json. The generated code imports
from this package, and Midnight releases move fast enough that a caret range here
would eventually pair generated code with a runtime it was not compiled against.
wallet-sdk requires >=1.2.0. Earlier versions leave the in-flight sync queue
effectively uncapped, so a wallet scanning a public chain from genesis grows until
the process dies with a heap out-of-memory error, minutes into a sync that looks
healthy until it stops. 1.2.0 exposes the caps that providers.ts sets. Do not relax
this bound.
shielded >=3.0.2 and facade >=4.1.0 are what expose those caps, so they move
together with wallet-sdk 1.2.
The `overrides` block collapses the two WebAssembly packages to ONE copy each, and it
is load-bearing. Each carries its own wasm instance owning its own classes, so an object
built by one copy fails the other's internal type check: 'expected instance of
LedgerParameters' and 'expected instance of StateValue'. Both surface from inside a
dependency, during a deployment, with nothing pointing at the duplication.
The duplication happens because midnight-js-protocol pins these two exactly (8.1.0 and
3.0.0) while everything else asks for a caret range, so npm nests a second copy the
moment a newer patch exists. The pinned versions satisfy every other declared range, so
the override picks a winner rather than forcing an unsupported combination.
Verify after any dependency change: `npm ls @midnight-ntwrk/ledger-v8` and
`npm ls @midnight-ntwrk/onchain-runtime-v3` must each report a single version. Neither
typecheck nor the simulator tests can see this - they never build a transaction.
